title: AI judges, expert iteration as RWR, and the SPIN loss
brief: Debias an AI judge, build self-rewarding preference pairs, prove expert iteration is reward-weighted regression on a toy, and implement SPIN exactly as its paper writes it.
hints: debias_judge averages two estimates of P(y1 wins): p_first_ab, and 1 - p_first_ba, since in the swapped order y1 is the second response shown.
preference_pairs: np.argmax and np.argmin return the first index among equal scores. Keep a row only when its max score is strictly above its min score.
filtered_sft_loss is -(rewards * seq_logps).sum() / rewards.sum(). Clamp the denominator to at least 1 so an all-zero batch gives 0, not nan. rwr_loss divides by the batch size B instead.
em_step: weight every one of the 4096 sequences by pi_old(y) * r(y), normalise, then for each step t add each weight to new[t, y_t] with np.add.at.
spin_loss: margin = lam * (policy_real - prev_real) - lam * (policy_synth - prev_synth), and ell(margin) = softplus(-margin). Return one value per pair, not the mean.
